items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: So I got a chance to meet him and talk with him,

ctx.x: Right, I remember. See, I was coming in -- I mean, I was coming in, and these guys were getting ready to go out, you know? And this was the thing. But I got a chance -- Jimmy Blyth was selling peanuts and popcorn at the Apollo Theatre on 47th Street. And they used to have -- they couldn't have a band, so they had piano players. And Jimmy Blyth used to play the pictures there. And then Tiny Parham played the pictures there.
So I got a chance to meet him and talk with him,

and then I used to listen to his records and all of that. But I was just the peanut and popcorn boy at that time. And then I would go and get a drum, it was just a snare drum, that's all I had, and then they would let me sit down there with them and play. Say, keep quiet, play quiet. No, that was my training grounds.
